body:
Retaining task state matters more than the backoff itself.

Without state retention, a retry after capacity failure often just replays the most expensive part of the run and makes the outage costlier than it needed to be.

The two things I'd want here are:
- retry with preserved execution context/checkpoint, not a soft restart
- one clear ceiling where the product stops being hopeful and says "this run is blocked by capacity, here's the last good state"

Otherwise users get the worst combo: delay plus duplicate spend.

We've seen the same pattern while building MartinLoop. The lesson keeps being the same: retries are only healthy when they carry forward evidence, not just optimism.

body:
Measured confirmation from Windows Desktop that the current capacity path violates the retained-state contract described here.

Codex Desktop `26.721.4979.0`, model `gpt-5.6-sol` (high), ran a turn for 1,501,434 ms (~25 minutes) and then recorded:

```text
type: task_complete
turn_id: 019fa62c-0b6f-7bf0-ba34-e09aad4b8277
last_agent_message: null
error.message: Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.
error.codex_error_info: server_overloaded
```

There was no retry, no retained-state pause, and no user-facing explanation. The Desktop UI displayed only a red failure icon. The user had to inspect the internal rollout to identify the cause.

This adds two concrete acceptance requirements:

1. `server_overloaded` must not terminalize a turn as `task_complete` with a null agent message.
2. After retry exhaustion, the UI must visibly pause and offer **Retry now**, **Continue retrying**, **Switch model and resume**, or **Cancel**.

A configuration setting should control whether Codex asks before switching, automatically selects the closest available model, keeps retrying the selected model, or stops with a visible notification. Completed tool calls must not be replayed when the turn resumes.

Additional current Codex Desktop reproduction: #41808. In this case, repeated `gpt-5.6-sol` capacity errors were followed by an automatic Goal status transition to `blocked` at the same timestamp, with no actual `update_goal(blocked)` call; later continuation turns still executed. This appears to connect this capacity-retry tracker with #36249 and #29370.

body:
Hello Codex team,

Thank you for the work you are putting into Codex. As a Pro subscriber who relies on it for long-running tasks, I would welcome the progress-preserving pause and automatic-resume behavior discussed here.

When temporary service capacity is unavailable, I would prefer the task to preserve its progress, enter a clear waiting state, and resume automatically when capacity returns. If automatic retries are exhausted, keeping the task resumable would be much more helpful than requiring me to reconstruct the work.

It would also help if notices clearly distinguished account usage limits, temporary service capacity, and connection failures, and explained whether work is continuing, paused, or needs action from me. Please also clarify how paid-plan priority applies during temporary capacity constraints.

Thank you for considering this feedback. Reducing manual restarts would make Codex much easier to rely on for sustained work.

Kind regards,
David

I have a reproduction that rules out the local Desktop process as the reason retries stopped.

The thread/Goal was running on a remote machine. I powered off my local computer at about 22:00 (UTC+8) on 2026-10-01. At about 22:17, the remote Goal hit `Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.` and remained stalled overnight. It did not resume on its own. At 13:52 (UTC+8) on 2026-10-02, I manually started a continuation, after which it resumed processing.

So in this case the persistent remote execution remained available, but a transient capacity error still required explicit user intervention to continue.
